question: विकारि तेषां राजेन्द्र सुदुष्करकरं मनः। ये पापानि न कुर्वन्ति मनोवाक्कर्मबुद्धिभिः। ते तपन्ति महात्मानो न शरीरस्य शोषणम्॥
answer: These high-souled, men who do not commit sin in word, in deed, in heart or in soul, are said (really) to perform asceticism; but not those who make their bodies emaciated by fasts and penances.

question: अपण्डितो वापि सुहृत् पण्डितो वाप्यनात्मवान्। नापरीक्ष्य महीपालः कुर्यात् सचिवमात्मनः॥
answer: Nor a friend who is not learned, nor a learned friend who has not his mind under control. a king should not appoint any body his own counselor without a trial.

question: तं चोपाध्यायः प्रेषयामास-'वत्सोपमन्यो! गा रक्षस्व' इति॥
answer: Him the preceptor thus addressed, “Go my child, look after my kine.

question: क्षुरप्रकृत्तौ सुभृशं सतोमरौ शुभाङ्गदौ चन्दनरूषितौ भुजौ। गजात् पतन्तौ युगपद युगपद विरेजतुयथाद्रिशृङ्गाद् रुचिरौ महोरगौ॥
answer: Those two arms, that were deeply cut by two razor-like shafts and that had two lances in their grasp and that had been adorned with the Angadas and also that had been smeared with soft sandal and again, having fallen from the back of the elephant at the same instant of time shone brightly even as two gigantic snakes after having dropped down from the summit of the mountain, shine (on the earth).

question: अद्यापि मुदिताः सन्तु सुहृदस्तेऽभिषेचने। अद्य भीताः पलायन्तु दुष्प्रदास्ते दिशो दश॥
answer: O noble one, to-day let your friends rejoice in consequence of your coronation. To day let those that intend to do you harm, being frightened, fly to the ten cardinal points.

question: बाहुभिः कवचैश्चिवैः शिरोभिश्चारुकुण्डलैः। युद्धोपकरणैश्चान्यैस्तत्र तत्र चकाशिरे॥
answer: Heroes, with pale countenances and with head graced with charming ear-rings and armed with the implements of war, appeared extremely resplendent.

question: राक्षसेन्द्रोऽपि विस्फार्य चापमिन्द्राशनिप्रभम्। निरन्तरमिवाकाशं कुर्वन्बाणांस्ततोऽसृजत्॥
answer: And stretching his bow resembling in splendour the thunderbolt of Indra, he discharged arrows covering up the sky.

question: ततः सर्वे द्विजवराः समाजग्मुः कृपान्विताः। स्वस्त्यात्रेयो महाजानुः कुशिकः शंखमेखलः॥
answer: Then there came all the noted Brahmanas, filled with compassion. Svastyatreya, Mahajanu, Kushika, Shankhamekhala.

question: पनसो नाम मेधावी वानरः सुमहाबलः। कोटीर्दश द्वादश च त्रिंशत् पञ्च प्रकर्षति॥
answer: The intelligent monkey, Panasa by name and endued with a vast strength collected together fifty two hundreds of millions (of monkeys).

question: चतुर्भिर्लक्षणीनं तथा षड्भिः सषोडशैः। पुरुषं तमतिक्रम्य आकाशं प्रतिपद्यते॥
answer: He becomes freed from the four means of perception, viz., Direct knowledge (through the senses), Revelation, Inference, and Intuition, the six conditions, (Hunger, Trust, Grief, Delusion, Disease, and Death), and also the other six and ten senses, attributes, viz., five breaths, the ten senses, and the mind. Transcending the Creator (Brahiman), he becomes at one with the One Supreme Soul.

question: नाराजके जनपदे स्वकं भवति कस्यचित्। मत्स्या इव जना नित्यं भक्षयन्ति परस्परम्॥
answer: In a kingless country a person hardly preserves his life; and like fishes people eat up one another.

question: अभ्याशस्थमहं मन्ये श्वेताश्वं कृष्णासारथिम्। स एष श्रूयते शब्दो गाण्डीवस्यामितौजसः॥
answer: I think myself to be very near to that one of white steeds whose charioteer in Krishna, inasmuch as I hear the twang of the bow Gandiva wielded by that one of infinite prowess.

question: शोकसंतप्तहृदया रुदती वेपती भृशम्। मणिपूरपतेर्माता ददर्श निहतं पतिम्॥
answer: Her heart burning with sorrow, weeping piteously the while, and trembling all over, the mother of the king of Manipura saw her killed husband.

question: धृष्टकेतुः कृपेणास्तान् छित्त्वा बहुविधाञ्छरान्। कृपं विव्याध सप्तत्या लक्ष्म चास्याहरत् त्रिभिः॥
answer: Dhristaketu having sundered in twain various shafts shot by Kripa, pierced the latter with seventy arrows; and then with three more cut-off the device on Kripa's standard.

question: नमो ज्येष्ठाय श्रेष्ठाय बलप्रमथनाय च। कालनाथाय कल्याय क्षयायोपक्षयाय च॥
answer: Salutations to you who are the eldest-born, who are the foremost of all creatures, and who are the crusher of the Asura Vala. Salutations to you who are the Master of Time, who are the personification of Kalpa; who are the embodiment of all kinds of destruction great and small.

question: व्याध उवाच न जीवनाशोऽस्ति हि देहभेदे मिथ्यैतदाहुर्मियते किलेति। जीवस्तु देहान्तरितः प्रयाति दशार्धतैवास्य शरीरभेदः॥
answer: The Fowler said : The spirit does not die, in death it simply has a change of abode. They are mistaken who foolishly say that all creatures are to die. The are never soul only goes to another body and its this change of abode is called the Death.

question: पञ्चमे त्वथ सम्प्राप्ते प्रथमे दिवसे गते। वराहसंस्थितं भूतं मत्समीपं समागमत्॥
answer: And when the first day of the fifth month had passed away, there appeared before me a being having the appearance of a boar,

question: तस्याः सा दीर्घबहुला वेपन्त्याः सीतया तदा। ददृशे कम्पिता वेणी व्यालीव परिसर्पती ॥
answer: And herself trembling, her pretty long lock of hair also shook and appeared like a serpent moving this way and that.

question: मुहूर्तमपि राम त्वां येऽनुपश्यन्ति केचन। पाविताः स्वर्गभूताश्च पूज्यास्ते त्रिदिवेश्वरैः॥
answer: O Rāma, one, who beholds you, even for a moment, becomes pure and worthy of repairing to heaven. Even the leading deities worship him.

question: ऋषयः पितरो देवा मनुष्या मृगपक्षिणः। यानि चान्यानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च॥ तपः परायणाः सर्वे सिद्ध्यन्ति तपसा च ते। इत्येवं तपसा देवा महत्त्वं प्रतिपेदिरे॥
answer: The Rishis, the gods, human beings, beasts, birds, and all other creatures, mobile or immobile, practise penances, and whatever success they acquire is won through penance. It was through penance that the gods acquired their superiority.

question: बहुशीर्षास्ततो नागाः शिरोभिर्जलसंततिम्। मुमुचुः पावकाभ्याशे सत्वराः क्रोधमूर्च्छिताः॥
answer: Many-headed snakes, becoming mad with anger, speedily scattered on the fire water from their many hoods.

question: शकुनिः प्रतिविन्ध्यं तु पराक्रान्तं पराक्रमी। अभ्यद्रवत राजेन्द्र मत्तः सिंह इव द्विपम्॥
answer: 0 king the greatly powerful Shakuni attacked 'the might Prativindhya as a lion attacks an infuriated elephant.

question: प्रहसन् देवकीपुत्रमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। एष प्रयात्याधिरथिः सात्यकेः स्यन्दनं प्रति॥
answer: Said these words to the son of Devaki with a simile-“(Behold!) the son of Adhiratha is making for the car of Satyaki.

question: तौ गदाभिहतैर्गात्रैः क्षणेन रुधिरोक्षितौ। प्रेक्षणीयतरावास्तां पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
answer: On being struck with each other's mace, they soon became bathed in blood and looked more beautiful like two blossoming Kinshukas.

question: द्विरात्रमन्तरे शूर उष्य राघवनन्दनः। वाल्मीकेराश्रमं पुण्यमगच्छद्वासमुत्तमम्॥
answer: Having spent two nights on his way he arrived at the holy and picturesque hermitage of the great ascetic Vālmīki.

question: यथाकामं यथोत्साहं यथाकालमरिंदम। सेविता विषयाः पुत्र यौवनेन मया तव॥
answer: O son, O chastiser of foes, I have enjoyed with your youth to the full extent of my desires and to the full limit of my powers and all according to their seasons.

question: तेषां तपःप्रभावेण पश्याद्यापि रघूत्तम। द्योतयन्ती दिशः सर्वाः श्रिया वेद्यतुलप्रभा॥
answer: Behold, O best of Raghus, this alter of incomparable beauty, by virtue of their asceticism, has been still shedding its lustre on all the sides.

question: इति रामेण सा प्रोक्ता राक्षसी काममोहिता। विसृज्य रामं सहसा ततो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्॥
answer: Having been thus addressed by Rāma, the Rākṣasī intoxicated with lust, at once leaving Rāma, spoke to Lakşmaņa.

question: तथा पाण्डुसुताः पार्थं चिह्नमात्रेण जज्ञिरे। तयोवरयोदृष्ट्वा तादृशं तं पराक्रमम्॥ विस्मयं सर्वभूतानि जग्मुर्भारत संयुगे। न तयोविवरं कश्चिद् रणे पश्यति भारत॥ धर्मेस्थितस्य हि यथा न कश्चिद् वृजिनं क्वचित्। उभौ च शरजालेन तावदृश्यौ बभूवतुः॥
answer: So could the Pandavas also come to Partha by recognising his standard alone. O king, seeing the prowess thus displayed by those two foremost of men, O descendant of Bharata, all persons in that great battle were filled with wonder. None marked any difference between the two. Both of them were perfectly invisible by their continuous showers of arrows.

question: मत्स्योऽन्यत्वं यथाज्ञानादुदकान्नाभिमन्यते। आत्मानं तद्वदज्ञानादन्यत्वं नैव वेदम्यहम्॥
answer: Indeed, like a fish that does not know anything else than water to be its element, I also have never known anything else than children and wives to be my own!

question: प्रवेष्टुं नात्र शक्ष्यामि धर्मो विग्रहवानृपः। सत्यवादी रणपटुः सर्वसत्त्वहिते रतः॥
answer: For king is the personification of virtue and specially the king Råma is truthful, well versed in the science of fighting and ever engaged in the welfare of all beings.

question: ततः संक्षोदयित्वा तामोषधीं वानरोत्तमः। लक्ष्मणस्य ददौ नस्तः सुषेणः सुमहाद्युतिः॥
answer: Then crushing the healing herb, that best of monkeys-the exceedingly effulgent Sușeņa, made Laksmana smell the same.

question: स ताड्यमानः प्रहसन् भक्षयामास वानरान्॥ बलं चण्डबलाख्यं च वल्लाबाहुं च वानरम्।
answer: Thus struck, he only laughed (at them) and fell to eating up the monkeys, named Bala, Chandabala and Vajrabahu.

question: भूत्वा मीनोऽष्ट वर्षाणि मृतो जायति भारत। मृगस्तु चतुरो मासांस्ततश्छागः प्रजायते॥
answer: Living as a fish for eight years he is born, O Bharata, as a deer. Living as a deer for four months he is next born as a goat.

question: सर्वलक्षणसंपन्ना सुरसा चैव भामिनी। अपत्यं तु मृगाः सर्वे मृग्या नरवरोत्तम॥
answer: And the beautiful Surasa of every auspicious sign. O best of men, the offspring of Mrigi are all beasts of deer species.

question: अद्याहवे यस्य न तुल्यमन्यं मन्ये मनुष्यं धनुराददानम्॥ सर्वामिमां यः पृथिवीं विजिग्ये तेन प्रयोद्धास्मि समेत्य संख्ये।
answer: Today, I will encounter in battle the man, who, in my view, is non-pariel amongst the archers and who conquered the entire earth.

question: बालोऽप्यबालः स्थविरो रिपुर्यः सदा प्रमत्तं पुरुषं निहन्यात्। कालेनान्यस्तस्य मूलं हरेत कालज्ञाता पार्थिवानां वरिष्ठः॥
answer: An enemy, whether he be a child, a young man, or an aged one, succeeds in killing a careless person. An insignificant enemy, when he becomes powerful, may root out a king. A king, therefore, who is conversant with the requirements of time is the greatest of all kings.

question: भीमसेन उवाच अर्जुनार्जुन बीभत्सो शृणुष्वैतद् वचो मम। यदर्थं क्षत्रिया सूते तस्य कालोऽयमागतः॥
answer: Bhimasena said Ho, Arjuna, Arjuna, O Vibhatsu, hear these words of mine! The hour, for the realisation of that object for which Kshatriya ladies bring forth their sons, has now arrived.

question: इत्युक्ते वचने तस्मिन् प्रद्युम्नेन तथा त्वहम्। प्रत्यब्रुवं महाराज यत् तच्छृणु समाहितः॥
answer: When Pradyuinna said, these words to me, I answered him as follows. Do you hear, O king, with rapt attention, what those words were.

question: सर्वरत्नसमाकीर्णे पुंसां देशे मनोरमे। इत्येवं धृतराष्ट्रस्य वचनाच्चक्रिरे कथाः॥
answer: The procession is the most grand in the world; and all gems and jewels (now) there delight the heart." Thus did they (counsellors) under instruction from Dhritarashtra, speak (of the city). O sons,

question: रक्षस्तु वाचं सम्पूज्य प्रश्नं पप्रच्छ तं द्विजम्। मोक्ष्येसे ब्रूहि मे प्रश्न केनास्मि हरिणः कृशः॥
answer: Respectfully saluting the Brahmana with words, the Rakshasa put to him this question: You shall escape, but tell me why I am so pale and lean.

question: जनमेजय उवाच कथं द्वादशवार्पिक्यामनावृष्ट्यां द्विजोत्तमान्। ऋषीनध्यापयामास पुरा सारस्वतो मुनिः॥
answer: Janamejaya said "Why did the sage Sarasvat, O you of ascetic merit, teach the Vedas to the Rishis during a twelve years' drought?

question: स्वस्त्रीयाभ्यां नरव्याघ्रो नाकम्पत यथाऽचलः। प्रहसन्निव तां चापि शस्त्रवृष्टिं जघान ह॥
answer: Shot by his nephews, that foremost of men (the Madra king) moved not, but stood still even like a mountain; then as if smiling, he baffled that shower of arrows.

question: ततः कृतज्ञं धर्मज्ञं रूपेणासदृशं भुवि। तपत्याः सदृशं मेने सूर्यः संवरणं पतिम्॥
answer: Thereupon Surya, seeing Samvarana, learned in the precepts of region and matchless in the world for his beauty, considered him to be the fittest husband for (his daughter) Tapati.

question: अद्यः वः सरथान् साश्वानशस्त्रो विरथोऽपि सन्। नक्षत्राणीव सर्वाणि सविता रात्रिसंक्षये॥
answer: Rising I shall fight all of you in battle Like the year that one by one meets with all the seasons, I shall meet with all of you in fight.

question: एवं सम्पूजितस्तत्र सुखमसम्युषितो नृप। इन्द्रस्य भवने पुण्ये गन्धर्वशिशुभिः सह॥
answer: Thus, O king, duly honoured, I dwelt cheerfully in the abode of Indra with the children of the Gandharvas.

question: शुभकृच्छुभमाप्नोति पापकृत्पापमश्नुते। विभीषणः सुखं प्राप्तस्त्वं प्राप्तः पापमीदृशम्।।२६
answer: The performer of the good receives good (result)-the perpetrator of the vicious (deeds) meets with bad (result). Vibhisana has attained to happiness and you have met with this your end.

question: अज्ञानात् तु कृतां हिंसामहिंसा व्यपकर्षति। ब्राह्मणाः शास्त्रनिर्देशादित्याहुर्ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
answer: The Brahmavadins hold, under the authority of what has been sanctioned in the Vedas, that all acts of injury committed in ignorance are made good by virtuous acts.

question: अन्यथा परिदृष्टानि कविभिर्दोषदर्शिभिः। अन्यथा परिवर्तन्ते वेगा इव नभस्वतः॥
answer: The act recommended to be followed by wise men competent to foresee the evil effects of actions have consequences other than those foreseen, like the winds from heaven (the direction taken by which no one can predict).

question: पटुघण्टाशतरवां वासवीमशनीमिव। निर्मुक्ताशीविषाकारां पृक्तां गजमदैरपि॥
answer: It produced sounds on account of the bells attached to it, like unto the thunder of Indra. It resembled in shape a dreadful serpent that had just cast off its slough, soaked with the temporal juice of elephants.

question: ततः सात्यकिमादाय पाणौ हार्दिक्यमेव च। ऋषिभिस्तैरनुज्ञातो निर्ययौ मधुसूदनः॥
answer: Then taking Satyaki by his hand and also the son of Hridika the slayer of Madhu went out, with the permission of those Rishis.

question: सहसाचरितां स्थानान्महीं पुण्यक्षयाद् गताम्। संहृतद्युतिविस्तारां तारामिव दिवश्च्युताम्॥
answer: Like a star on the expiration of its virtue, moving from its place and dislodged from heaven, dropping to the earth with its brightness contracted.

question: ततो यथेष्टमगमत् पुनरेव स केसरी। ततः समुद्रतीरेण वङ्गान् पुण्ड्रान् सकोसलान्॥
answer: The sacrificial horse then, having beautiful manes, proceeded at his will along the seacoast, going to the countries of the Bangas, the Pundras, and the Kosalas.

question: सायुधाः सगदाश्चैव सखगाः सपरश्वधाः। सप्रासकवचाश्चान्ये नराः सुप्ताः पृथक् पृथक्॥
answer: Others soldiers, well-armed and with maces, swords, axes and lances in grasp and covered with coats of mail, laid themselves down separately.

question: एतत् प्रत्यक्षतः सर्वं पूर्वं वृत्तं द्विजोत्तम। तस्मादिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं सर्वहेत्वात्मिकां कथाम्॥ अनुभूतं हि बहुशस्त्वयैकेन द्विजोत्तमा न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचित् सर्वलोकेषु नित्यदा॥
answer: O foremost of Brahmanas, you have seen with your own eyes all that happened before. You alone have seen many things by your senses. There is nothing in all the world that is not known to you. Therefore, I eagerly desire to hear all about things.

question: स्थापनं चाकरोद् विष्णुः स्वयमेव सनातनः। नातिवर्तिष्यते कश्चिद् राजंस्त्वामिति भारत॥
answer: The eternal Vishnu himself, O Bharata, confirmed his power, telling him,-No one, O king, shall excel you.

question: आत्मा जेयः सदा राज्ञा ततो जेयाश्च शत्रवः। अजितात्मा नरपतिविजयेत कथं रिपून्॥
answer: The king should first conquer himself and then try to subdue his enemies. He can a king who has not been able to conquer his own self be able to conquer his enemies?

question: न हि ते वृजिनं किंचिद् वर्तते परमण्वपि। अस्मिन् मार्गे निषीदेयुः सेन्द्रा अपि सुरासुराः॥
answer: (By following this path) you have not incurred even an atom of sin. The gods together with Indra and the Asuras have (sometimes) to adopt this path.

question: अभीषाहाञ्छूरसेनान् बाह्रीकान् सवसातिकान्। निकृत्य पृथिवीं राजा चक्रे शोणितकर्दमाम्॥
answer: Chopping off the Abhishahas, the Surasenas, the Valhikas and the Vashatikas, he made the earth muddy with (their) flesh and blood.

question: नृशंस इति मां राम वक्ष्यन्ति मनुजा भुवि॥ श्रुत्वा तस्यागुणान्सर्वे वक्ष्यन्ति सुकृतं पुनः।
answer: O Rāma, perhaps people of this earth will call me cruel but they will again recognise my act as good when they will hear of his vicious deeds.

question: अभिद्रुत्य तु राधेयः पाण्डुपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥ वज्रच्छत्रांकुशैर्मतस्यैर्ध्वजकूर्मम्बुजादिभिः। लक्षणैरुपपन्नेन पाण्डुना पाण्डुनन्दनम्॥ पवित्रीकर्तुमात्मानं स्कन्धे संस्पृश्य पाणिना। ग्रहीतुमिच्छन् स बलात् कुन्तीवाक्यं च सोऽस्मरत्॥
answer: It seemed at the time when Karna, the son of Radha was chasing Yudhishthira as if he is intended to catch him forcibly so as to touch him on should with his fair colour hand having lucky marks as thunderbolt, umbrella, goad, fish, flag, tortoise and lotus etc. in order to attain purity. In the meantime, a memory of commitment he had made once before Kunti, chained his racing feet.

question: द्रवमाणान् रथोदारान् किरन्तं निशितैः शरैः॥ नैनं शक्ष्यामि संसोढुं चरन्तं रणमूर्धनि।
answer: Crushing numerous illustrious car-warriors and covering them with his sharp shafts I cannot brook the sight of him careering in thick of the fight.

question: महावराहं तं देवं सर्वलोकपितामहम्। अहं चैव नमस्यामि नित्यमेव जगत्पतिम्॥
answer: I, too, vow my head in respect to that Lord of the universe, that Grandfather of all the worlds, that powerful and huge boar.

question: वृष्ण्यन्धकविनाशाय किंकरप्रतिमं महत्॥ असूत शापजं घोरं तच्च राज्ञे न्यवेदयन्।
answer: Indeed, for the destruction of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas, Shambas brought forth, through that curse, a dreadful iron bolt that looked like a huge messenger of death. The fact was duly reported to the king.

question: पुनः पुनस्तूबरक मूढ औदरिकेति च। अकृतास्रक मा योत्सीर्बाल संग्रामकातर॥ इति मामब्रवीत् कर्णः पश्यतस्ते धनंजय। एवं वक्ता च मे वध्यस्तेन चोक्तोऽस्मि भारत॥
answer: "O Dhananjaya, in your very presence, Karna has repeatedly said to me-(you are) a eunuch, fool, child, glutton, (you are) unable to endure (the fury of) battle. He, that would tell me so, would be my victim. O Bharata, he (Karna) has said to me these words (and therefore, he must be slain by me),

question: एवं सर्वमशेषेण रावणान्तःपुरं कपिः। ददर्श स महातेजा न ददर्श च जानकीम्॥
answer: Thus that highly energetic monkey saw everything thoroughly in the inner apartment of Ravana, but he saw not Janaka's daughter.

question: त्वां हि प्राप्य रणे क्षत्रमेकाहादिति भारत॥ नश्यमानमहं युक्तं मन्येयमिति मे मतिः।
answer: O Bharata, methinks, it would not appear impossible even if all the Kshatriyas were to be exterminated in the course of a day, with you for their adversary in the field.

question: असह्यं सर्वभूतानां ममापि विपुलं बलम्। मयापि सुमहत् कर्म कृतं दैतेयविग्रहे॥
answer: My great strength too is unendurable by all creature and by me too have been done great deeds in the war the sons of Diti.

question: सर्वथा न हि मे पुत्राः सहामात्याः ससौबलाः। क्रुद्ध पार्थे च भीमे च वासुदेवे च सात्वते॥
answer: When these Bhima, Partha (Arjuna) and Vasudeva (Krishna) of the Satvata race are angry, my sons with their friends and the son of Subala are surely not at all capable to fight with them.

question: यदाश्रौषं कलहद्यूतमूलं मायाबलं सौबलं पाण्डवेन। हतं संग्रामे सहदेवेन पापं तदा नाशंसे विजयाय संजय॥
answer: I had no hope of success, O Sanjaya, when I heard that Saubala, the man of magic power and the root of the gaming and the feud, had been killed by Sahadeva.

question: भवतस्तां सभां दृष्ट्वा समृद्धिं चाप्यनुत्तमाम्। दुर्योधनस्तदाऽऽसीनः सर्वं पित्रे न्यवेदयत्॥
answer: Having seen that grand palace and that great prosperity of yours, Duryodhana, while sitting before his father described to him of all he had seen.

question: अथायान्तं हनूमन्तं ददर्शक्षपतिस्तदा। वानरैः कृतसंग्रामैः श्वसद्भिरभिसंवृतम्॥
answer: Then the lord of bears saw Hanumān approach, surrounded by monkeys sighing hard, who had faught the fight.

question: ऐश्वर्यं वै महद् ब्रह्म वर्णे कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितम्। निवर्तते चापि पुनः कथमैश्वर्यमुत्तमम्॥
answer: Upon which order (of men) has been placed high Brahma prosperity? In what manner, again, does high prosperity fall off?

question: वृष्टिमारुतसंतापैः सुखैः स्थावरजङ्गमान्। वर्धयन् सुमहातेजाः पुनः प्रतिनिवर्तते॥
answer: And having nourished all (creatures) both mobile and immobile by the comfort caused by rain, wind and warmth, that one of mighty splendour resumes his (former) course.

question: ददर्शोष्णोदकैः पूर्णा नदीं चापि सुदुर्गमाम्। असिपत्रवनं चैव निशितं क्षुरसंवृतम्॥
answer: He saw a river full of boiling water and therefore difficult to cross as also a forest of trees whose leaves were sharp swords and razors.

question: संस्कृतं प्रसवं याति स्वल्पमन्नं चतुर्विधम्। अक्षय्यं वर्धते चान्नं तेन भोजयते द्विजान्॥
answer: The food, however little that was cooked, becoming four kinds increased and become inexhaustible. Who them he (Yudhishthira) fed the Brahman.

question: तेन शूद्रानशेषेण ब्रह्मस्थानादपाकृतः। ब्राह्मणः शूद्रतामेति नास्ति तत्र विचारणा॥
answer: On account of those remains of a Shudra's food in his stomach, he falls away from the position of a Brahmana. Such a Brahmana becomes surely a Shudra.

question: न मन्ये ब्रह्मचर्ये वा स्वधीते वा फलोदयः। मार्दवार्जवयोर्वापि त्वां चेद् व्यसनमागतम्॥
answer: I deem the Brahmacarya mode of life, or study, or meekness or sincerity as attended with no fruit, since you have come by calamity.

question: यस्य कोशश्च दण्डश्च मित्राण्यात्मा च भूमिप। समान्येतानि सर्वाणि स राज्यं महदश्नुते॥
answer: O king, truly does he attain to a vast kingdom, who has the same wealth, soldiery and body with his friends.

question: संजय उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा स यन्तारमचोदयत्। सुमित्राश्वान् रणे क्षिप्रं द्रोणानीकाय चोदया॥
answer: Sanjaya said Hearing those words of Yudhishthira, Abhimanyu commanded his charioteer saying-"Quickly urge, O Sumitra, the steeds towards Drona's divisions."

question: तत उत्थाय कैकेयी सर्वास्ताः प्रत्यभाषत। प्रेष्याः समुत्थिताश्चापि कैकेयीं ताः स्त्रियोऽब्रुवन्॥ प्रेक्ष्य मामनवद्यागी कश्मलोपहतामिव। स्नेहात् संवासजाद् धर्मात् सूदमेषा शुचिस्मिता॥ योद्ध्यमानं महावीर्यमियं समनुशोचति। कल्याणरूपा सैरन्ध्री बल्लवश्चापि सुन्दरः॥ स्त्रीणां चित्तं च दुर्जेयं युक्तरूपौ च मे मतौ। सैरन्ध्री प्रियसंवासान्नित्यं करुणवादिनी॥ अस्मिन् राजकुले चेमौ तुल्यकालनिवासिनौ। इति ब्रुवाणा वाक्यानि सा मां नित्यमतर्जयत्॥
answer: Then rising from her seat along with her maids who also rose up with her, Kaikayi beholding me with limbs uninjured and only overtaken by swoon, addressed them saying "surely it is from the affection originated by living together that this lady of beautiful smile grieves for the cook, seeing him fighting with beasts of exceeding strength. Sairandhri is one of exceeding beauty and Ballava is handsome too, the heart of woman is so hard to know; and me-thinks they both are deserving of each other. Sairandhri is seen constantly lamenting for the connection with her lover and they both have entered this royal family at the same time.” Speaking such words she always scolds me.

question: के भवन्तोऽवलम्बन्ते गर्ने ह्यस्मिन्नधोमुखाः। वीरणस्तम्बके लग्नाः सर्वतः परिभक्षिते॥ मूषकेन निगूढेन गर्तेऽस्मिन्नित्यवासिना।
answer: “Who are you thus hanging in the hole, your heads downward, by a rope of the Virana fibre which has been eaten by the rats that live secretly near this hole?"

question: वैशम्पायन उवाच स राजा सुमहातेजा वृद्धः कुरुकुलोद्वहः॥ न ददर्श तदा किंचिदप्रियं पाण्डुनन्दने।
answer: Vishampayana said Endued with great energy, that perpetuator of Kuru's race, viz., the old king Dhritarashtra, could not see any ill-will in Yudhishthira.

question: लोमश उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा विरराम बन्दी। श्लोकस्यार्धं व्याजहाराष्टवक्रः।
answer: Lomasha said : Having said this Bandi stopped. Thereupon Ashtavakra supplied the other half of the Sloka.

question: स तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा वानरस्य महात्मनः। आज्ञापयद् वधं तस्य रावणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥
answer: Hearing the words of the high-souled monkey, Răvaņa, bereft of his senses by wrath, ordered that he should be put to death.

question: अलर्क उवाच स्पृष्ट्वा त्वग्विविधान् स्पर्शी स्तानेव प्रतिगृध्यति। तस्मात् त्वचं पाटयिप्ये विविधैः कङ्कपत्रिभिः॥
answer: Alarka said The skin, touching various objects of touch, hankers after them only. Hence, I shall tear off the skin with various arrows equipt with the feathers of the Kanka.

question: ब्राह्मणैः सहिता वीरा ह्यवसन् पुरुषर्षभाः। कृष्णायास्तत्र पश्यन्तः क्रीडितान्यमरप्रभाः। विचित्राणि नरव्याघ्रा रेमिरे तत्र पाण्डवाः॥
answer: Those foremost of men, those heroes then lived there with the Brahmanas. Those best of men, the celestials-like Pandavas, seeing the various scenes with Krishna (Draupadi) derived great pleasure.

question: सुखं प्राप्स्यसि कल्याणि पाण्डवान् प्राप्य वै पतीन्। इति दुपदराजेन पित्रा दत्ताऽऽयतेक्षणा॥
answer: This large-eyed lady was bestowed on us by her father, the king of Drupada, in the hope that this blessed damsel would be happy by obtaining the Pandavas as her husbands.

question: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा वदति वार्ष्णेयेधर्मराजे च भारता अथ पश्चात् तपोवृद्धो बहुवर्षसहाधृक्॥ प्रत्यदृश्यतधर्मात्मा मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः। अजरश्चामरश्चैव रूपौदार्यगुणान्वितः॥
answer: Vaishampayana said: O Bharata, when the descendant of the Vrishnis and the Dharmaraja were thus conversing, the high-souled Markandeya, of great devotion, grown wise by austerities, who had lived many thousands of years, was seen to approach (there). Being immortal and without signs of senility, endued with beauty and magnanimity.

question: क्षिप्रमेष्यति ते भर्ता सुग्रीवेणाभिरक्षितः। सौमित्रिसहितो धीमांस्त्वां चेतो मोक्षयिष्यति॥
answer: Your intelligent husband accompanied by the son of Sumitra and protected by Sugriva will soon arrive (here) and deliver you hence.

question: गदा क्षिप्ता तु समरे मद्रराजेन भारत। व्योम दीपयमाना सा ससृजे पावकं मुहुः॥
answer: The mace hurled by the king of the Madras in battle, O Bharata, illuminating the welkin, frequently emitted flashes of fires.

question: कुमारा ऊचुः मुद्रिकामपि विप्रर्षे शीघ्रमेतां समुद्धर।
answer: The princes said : "O best of the twice born, raise up the ring without delay.

question: दारयन् बहुधा सैन्यं रणे चरति कालवत्। यत्रैष शब्दस्तुमुलस्तत्र सूत रथं नय॥
answer: O charioteer, drive my car to the spot whence this noise is coming. Surely Yuyudhana has now encountered these heroes that fight with the stones.

question: वधार्थं वयमायातास्तस्य वै मुनिभिः सह ॥ सिद्धगन्धर्वयक्षाश्च ततस्त्वां शरणं गताः। त्वं गतिः परमा देव सर्वेषां नः परंतप ॥
answer: It is to compass his death that accompanied by the ascetics, we have come here: it is for this that the Siddhas and the Gandharvas and the Yaksas have taken refuge in you! O God, you are the prime way of us all, O repressor of foes! Do you, for bringing destruction to the enemies of the gods, turn your thoughts to being born as man.

question: प्रतिगृह्य च सत्कारैरर्घ्यपाद्यादिकं वरम्। पृष्टश्चागमने हेतुमुवाच विनतासुतः॥
answer: Having accepted the usual warm welcome and Arghya a and water for washing the feet etc. they were asked the reason of their coming and the son of Vinata thus explained the reasons:

question: तस्यां चोत्पादयामास विदुरः कुरुनन्दनः। पुत्रान् विनयसम्पन्नानात्मनः सदृशान् गुणैः॥
answer: The descendant of Kuru, Vidura, begot on her children as gentle and accomplished as he himself was.

question: तस्माच्चरेथाः सततं क्षमाशीलो जितेन्द्रियः। क्षमया प्राप्स्यसे लोकान्ब्रह्मणः समनन्तरान्॥
answer: Therefore, you should always live, being forgiving in your temper and self-controlling of your passions. By forgiveness you will attain to worlds that are beyond the reach of even Brahma.

question: नूनं मित्राणि ते रक्षः साधूपचरितान्यपि। स्वदोषादपरज्यन्ते तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
answer: Indeed, O Rakshasa, your friends thought welltreated by you are still not welldisposed towards you on account of their own vicious nature. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

question: आवृत्य तु महाबाहुर्यतो द्रौणिस्ततो हयान्। अन्तरं प्रददौ पार्थो द्रोणस्य व्यपसर्पितुम्॥
answer: Then turning his horses towards Drona's son, Partha offered Drona an opportunity to retreat.

question: पूर्णे शतसहस्रे तु विप्राणां परिविष्यताम्। स्थापिता तत्र संज्ञाभूच्छलो ध्मायति नित्यशः॥
answer: When (full) one lac Brahmanas were every day fed, it was arranged (to notify) the fact by blowing conchs in a chorus.

question: विद्याधरा मदक्षीवा मदरक्तान्तलोचनाः। योषिद्भिःसह संक्रान्ताश्चिक्रीडुर्जहषुश्च वै॥
answer: There danced mirthfully, with their damsels, the Vidyādharas, inebriate and having their eyes reddened with drink.

question: अपेयः सागरो येषामपि शापान्महात्मनाम्। येषां कोपाग्निरद्यापि दण्डके नोपशाम्यति॥
answer: Through the curse of those great ones, the ocean become so saline as to be undrinkable. The fire of their anger yet burns in the forest of Dandaka, unquenched by time.

question: तदिदं ह्यन्यथाभूतं व्यवदीर्णं मनो मम। पितरं यो न पश्यामि नित्यं प्रियहिते रतम्॥
answer: But it has fallen out otherwise. That I do not behold my father ever engaged in the dear welfare (of his subjects) cleaves my heart mother.

question: तत्र होता बभूवाथ ब्राह्मणश्चण्डभार्गवः। च्यवनस्यान्वये ख्यातो जातो वेदविदां वरः॥
answer: The Brahmana, named Chanda Bhargava, born in the race of Chyavana, greatly illustrious and the foremost man amongst all the learned in the Vedas, became the Hota in that sacrifice.

question: ब्राह्मणा बलमुख्याश्च नैगमाश्चागतास्त्विह॥ दर्शनं तेऽभिकाङ्क्षन्ते प्रतिबुद्ध्यस्व राघव।
answer: Brāhmaṇas, commanders and merchants are assembled at the palace gate, desirous of seeing you, do you therefore arise, Oh descendant of Raghu.

question: न गोप्स्यति दुराचारः स आत्मानं कथंचन॥ तत्र छिद्रे प्रहर्तव्यं त्वयास्य कुरुसत्तम।
answer: That wicked creature will no longer conceal himself. Taking advantage of that opportunity you should, O foremost of the Kurus, strike him.

question: त्वमत्र हेतुं जानीषे तस्मात् सत्यं निरुच्यताम्। रहस्यं यदि ते नास्ति किंचिदत्र वदस्व नः॥
answer: You are (undoubtedly) aware of the cause of this. Therefore speak truly. If you have nothing to conceal, then relate it to us.

question: अन्योन्यं नातिवर्तन्ते सम्यक् च भवति द्विजा यदा तु विषमं भावमाचरन्ति चराचराः॥ तदा देही देहमन्यं व्यतिरोहति कालतः। आनुपूर्व्या विनश्यन्ति जायन्ते चानुपूर्वशः॥
answer: O Brahmana, they are not opposed to one another; they exist in proper combination. When this universe is thrown into a state of chaos then every corporeal being in proper time assumes another body. It perishes also in due order.

question: नाशयन्तीव मे प्राणान् यमदूता इवाहिताः॥ गदापरिघसंस्पर्शा नेमे बाणाः शिखण्डिनः।
answer: Of touch heavy like that of a mace or a bludgeon these arrows are destroying my vital breaths like so many messengers of Death. Surely they are not Shikhandin's.

question: यदि त्वं यास्यसि वनं त्यक्त्वा मां शोकलालसाम्। अहं प्रायमिहासिष्ये न च शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्॥
answer: If do you depart to the forest leaving me troubled with sorrow, I shall resort to the vow of fasting and shall not be able to sustain my life.

question: अहं तु तद् विजानामि विजेतुं येन शक्यते। युधिष्ठिरं स्वयं राजंस्तन्निबोध जुषस्व च॥
answer: But I know the means by which Yudhishthira may be vanquished. O king, listen to it and adopt it.

question: तावब्रूतां वृणीष्वेति तदा भरतसत्तम। अथैतावब्रवीच्छक्रः साह्यं नः क्रियतामिति॥
answer: Those two then said “Choose (the boon)," O best of the race of Bharata. Shakra then said to those two-"make us invincible".

question: कः शक्तस्तस्य देवस्य ख्यातस्य स्वेन कर्मणा। तादृशं प्रतिकुर्वीत अंशेनापि नृपात्मज॥
answer: O king's son, who is capable of repaying even in part an action like that of the divine (Rāma) renowned by means of his own acts?

question: ततः प्रवृत्तः संग्राम: समीपे लवणाम्भसः। सुराणामसुराणां च सर्वघोरतरो महान्॥
answer: Thus began the terrible battle between the Devas and Danavas on the shores of the salt sea.

question: इत्युक्त्वा रथमास्थाय रौहिणेयः प्रतापवान्। श्वेताभ्रशिखराकारः प्रययौ द्वारकां प्रति॥
answer: Having said these words, the brave son of Rohini, looking like a white cloud, got upon his chariot and went towards Dwaraka.

question: अत उर्ध्वं निबोधेदं देवानां यष्टुमिच्छताम्। समागमे महाराज ब्रह्मणा वै स्वयम्भुवा॥
answer: After this, listen to what I would say. Once on a time the gods, desirous of making a Sacrifice, went, O king, to the presence of the Self-create Brahman.

question: सर्वे च ते बाष्पकलाः साश्रुनेत्रा विचेतसः। संमूढा इव दुःखेन त्यजन्तो राघवं तदा॥
answer: And other monkeys and Rākşasas were all moved with tears and sorrow to take leave of Rāma,

question: नूनं ममैव शोकेन स वीरो लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। देवलोकमितो यातस्त्यक्त्वा देहं महीतले॥
answer: Or renouncing his body on this earth for my grief, the heroic elder brother of Lakşmaņa, has repaired to the celestial region.

question: इदानीं तावदेवासौ मया दृष्टः कथं मृतः॥ इति कालेन ह्रियतां प्रलापः श्रूयते नृणाम्।
answer: Time carries away one and men say-I saw him a little while before How has he died?'

question: तत्र होनकपायत्तं राज्ञो भवति भारत। शाखानगरमर्हस्तु सहस्रपतिरुत्तमः॥
answer: Such a village, so given to a lord of a hundred villages, should be, however, with the jurisdiction of the chief of a thousand villages. That high officer, again, viz., the lord of a thousand villages, should have a small town for his support.

question: उदीच्याः कृतवर्मा च पुरुमित्रः सुतापनः। दुःशासनो निकुम्भश्च कुण्डभेदी पराक्रमः॥
answer: And the warriors of the North, Kritavarma, the sons of Purumitra, Dusasana, Nikumva, Kundavedi, Purukrama.

question: तुल्यं मम सहस्रं तु सुतानां ब्रह्मवादिनाम्। आयुश्चैव सपुत्रस्य संवत्सरशतायुतम्॥
answer: He also conferred upon me a thousand solis, all possessed of equal merit and fully conversant with the Vedas. Through his favour their periods of life as also mine have become extended to ten millions of years.

question: तां भक्त्वा स महाशाखां स्मयमानो विलोकयन्। अथात्र लम्बतोऽपश्यद्वालखिल्यानधोमुखान्॥ ॥
answer: As he cast his eyes in wonder on the broken branch of the tree, he saw that the Valakhilya Rishis were hanging form it, with their heads downwards.

question: हिरण्यकशिपोः पूर्वं मम पूर्वपितामहात्। न तस्य कालो मृत्युर्वा न व्याधिर्न विहिंसकाः॥ न दिवा मरणं तस्य न रात्री संध्ययोर्नहि। न शुष्केण न चाट्टैण न च शस्त्रेण केनचित्॥ विद्यते राक्षसश्रेष्ठ तस्य नास्त्रेण केनचित्। प्रह्लादेन समं चक्रे वादं परमदारुणम्॥ तस्य वादे समुत्पन्ने धीरो लोकभयंकरः। सर्ववर्यस्य वीरस्य प्रह्लादस्य महात्मनः॥ उत्पन्नो राक्षसश्रेष्ठ नृसिंहाकृतिरूपधृक्। दृष्टं च तेन रौद्रेण क्षुब्धं सर्वमशेषतः॥
answer: Formerly none bore enmity towards my ancestor Hiranyakasipu, Time Death, or illness. He had no death during the day, night, evening or morning. O foremost of Rākşasas, he did not experience death from any weapon whatsoever. He created a dreadful enmity with Prahlada. This conflict having taken place with the high-souled and heroic Prahlāda there rose up a dreadful figure of manlion, a terror to all, O foremost of Raksasas. And that terrible figure casting his looks about, all the worlds were over-whelmed.

question: तादृशो बध्यते बालो यत्र सत्यमनिष्ठितम्। सत्यानृते विनिश्चित्य ततो भवति धर्मवित्॥
answer: That ignorant person commits sin, who says truth which is not righteous. That person is a master of duties who can distinguish truth from untruth.

question: अथास्य बुद्धिरभवत् पुनरन्या तदा किला सृष्टाः प्रजा इमाः सर्वा ब्रह्मणा परमेष्ठिना॥ दैत्यदानवगन्धर्वरक्षोगणसमाकुला। जाता हीयं वसुमती भाराकान्ता तपस्विनी।॥
answer: After the work of Creation, however, had been done by Brahman, another thought arose in the mind of Narayana. Indeed,. He thought thus,-Brahman, otherwise called Parameshthi, has created all these creatures, consisting of Daityas and Danavas and Gandharvas and Rakshasas. The helpless Earth has become loaded with the weight of creatures.

question: ब्राह्मण उवाच इन्द्रियाणि तु यान्याहुः कानि तानि यतव्रत। निग्रहश्च कथं कार्यो निग्रहस्य च किं फलम्॥ कथं च फलमाप्नोति तेषां धर्मभृतां वर। एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन धर्मं ज्ञातुं निबोध मे॥
answer: The Brahmana said: O foremost of all virtuous and vowobserving men, you talk of the senses; what are they? How might they be subdued? What is the good of subduing them? How does a creature obtain the fruits of doing it? I eagerly desire to kuow all about these matters.

question: यदा त्वया सभार्येण संसुप्तो न प्रबोधितः। अहं तदैव ते प्रीतो मनसा राजसत्तम॥
answer: You, however, with your wife, did not awake me. Even then, O best of kings, I became delighted with you.

question: हा ममार्ये क्व यातासि हा साध्वि वरवर्णिनि॥ हा सकामाद्य कैकेयी देवि मेऽद्य भविष्यतु ।
answer: O chaste one, O you of exquisitely fine hue, O worshipful madam, whither have you repaired? O Sītă, truly has the desire of Kaikeyi been fulfilled to-day.

question: स भीमसेनाभिहत:सूतपुत्रः कुरूद्वह। निषसाद रथोपस्थे विसंज्ञः पृतनापतिः॥
answer: O descendant of Kuru, thus struck by Bhimasena, the Commander Suta's son sat down senseless on the terrace of his car.

question: षडपध्वंसजाश्चापि कानीनापसदास्तथा। इत्येते वै समाख्यातास्तान् विजानीहि भारत॥
answer: The son born of a maiden in her father's house is called Kanina. Besides these, there are six kinds of sons called Apadhwansaja and six others that are called Apasadas. These are the several kind of sons mentioned in the scriptures, know, O Bharata. are

question: संजय उवाच ततो युयुत्सुः कौरव्यान् परित्यज्यसुतांस्तव। जगाम पाण्डुपुत्राणां सेनां विश्राव्य दुन्दुभिम्॥
answer: Sanjaya said Then abandoning the Kurus, your son, Yuyutsu, went over to the army of the Pandavas with the best of drums and cymbals.

question: कृत्वा हि पूर्वं मित्राणि यः पश्चान्नानुतिष्ठति। न स मित्राणि लभते कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु दुर्मतिः॥
answer: Having made friends, he who forgets them afterwards, is a wicked person and never gets friends at times of danger and necessity.

question: यदाऽऽयाज्जलदप्रख्यो रथः परमवीर्यवान्। पर्जन्य इव वीभत्सुस्तुमुलामशनीं सृजन्॥
answer: As that mighty car-warrior of excessive energy, Vibhatsu, resembling a dense mass of rain-clouds, came, creating terrible sounds like the clappings of the thunder-bolt, like Parjanya itself.

question: गात्रेषु वलयः प्राप्ताः श्वेताश्चैव शिरोरुहाः। जरया पुरुषो जीर्णः किं हि कृत्वा प्रभावयेत्॥
answer: The person is filled with folds in the skin, the hair has grown hoary, the individual is enfeebled because of age, by doing what, can be prevent this?

question: स तु संहष्टसर्वाङ्गः प्राकारस्थो महाकपिः। पुष्पिताग्रान् वसन्तादौ ददर्श विविधान् दुमान्॥ सालानशोकान् भव्यांश्च चम्पकांश्च सुपुष्पितान्। उद्दालकान् नागवृक्षांश्चूतान् कपिमुखानपि ॥ तथाऽऽम्रवणसम्पन्नांल्लताशतसमन्वितान्। ज्यामुक्त इव नाराचः पुप्लुवे वृक्षवाटिकाम्॥
answer: All his frame filled with delight, that mighty monkey, stationed on the wall, saw various trees having their tops furnished with flowers through spring and the other seasons, salas and Asokas, bhavyas, champakas, uddalakas, and Nāgas, and those bearing fruits resembling the mouths of monkeys; and those relative to mango woods, with hundreds of plants. And (Hanuman) leapt into the garden like an arrow let go from the bow string.

question: प्रमोहो भ्रम आवर्तो प्राणं श्रवणदर्शने। अद्भुतानि रसस्पर्शे शीतोष्णे मारुताकृतिः॥ प्रतिभामुपसर्गाश्चाप्युपसंगृह्य योगतः। तांस्तत्त्वविदनादृत्य आत्मन्येव निवर्तयेत्॥
answer: Acquiring by Yoga annihilation, extension, power to present different shapes in the same person or body, celestial scents, and sounds, and sights, the most agreeable sensations of taste and touch, pleasurable sensations of coolness and warmth, equality with the wind, power to understanding the meaning of scriptures and every work of genius, living with celestial damsels, the Yogin should not care for them and merge them all in the Understanding.

question: अन्तर्धाय महाशब्दान् कर्णेनमिततेजसा॥ दोधूयमानस्य भृशं धनुषः शृणु निःस्वनम्।
answer: Karna, of unfathomable prowess, has drawn his bow and its loud twang can be heard above all other sounds.

question: निर्मासैरस्थिभूयिष्ठैर्गात्रैःस्नायुनिबन्धनैः। किं विशेष प्रपश्यन्ति तत्र तेषां परे जनाः॥ येन प्रत्यवगच्छेयुः कुलरूपविशेषणम्। कस्मादन्योन्यमिच्छन्ति विप्रलब्धधियो नराः॥
answer: Since the wise and the ignorant the rich and the poor, all, shorn of their anxieties, sleep on the crematorium, with bodies devoid of flesh and full of naked bones, and sinews, whom amongst them will the survivors regard as possessed of distinguishing marks by which the attributes of birth and beauty may be determined? Since every thing is equal in death why should men, whose understandings are always deceived covet one another's rank and position.

question: नावमन्यामि ते बुद्धिं नावमन्ये च पौरुषम्। नावमन्ये जयामिति जितवद् वर्ततां भवान्।॥
answer: I honour you intelligence, and I honour your power. I do not disregard you, saying that I have conquered you. On the other hand, live you with me as a victor.

question: नारदस्तु महातेजा मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थितः। चिन्तयामास विप्रेन्द्रो विधूम इव पावकः॥
answer: The exceedingly energetic Nārada best of Brāhmaṇas resembling a smokeless fire, remaining rapt for a while, began to reflect.

question: तथा शरीरं भवति देहाद् येनोपपादितम्। अध्वानं गतकशायं प्राप्तश्चायं गृहाद् गृहम्॥
answer: He who having obtained a body, destroys it himself becomes invested with another body of a similar nature. Though set on the path of Liberation, he yet becomes a traveller and acquires another body like a person going from one room into another.

question: तं चेद् द्विजमुपागच्छेद् वर्तमानं स्वकर्मणि। अकुर्वाणं विक्रर्माणि शान्तं प्रज्ञानतर्पितम्॥ कुर्वीतापत्यसंतानमथो दद्याद् यजेत च। संविभज्य च भोक्तव्यं धनं सद्भिरितीर्यते॥
answer: If while engaged in the observance of his own duties, without doing any unfair act, riches comes to a peaceful Brahmana endued with knowledge, he should then marry and seek to beget children, and should also practise charity and celebrate sacrifices. It has been declared by the wise that wealth thus acquired should be enjoyed by distributing it among worthy persons and relatives.

question: इदं च यदि वा मोहाल्लोभाद्वा व्याहृतं मया। तत्रापि च महाराज न दोषं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
answer: If I have said this through ignorance or covetousness, you ought not, O mighty monarch, criminate me.

question: प्रकाशरूपस्तु यदा न शक्तस्तौ बाधितुं राक्षराजपुत्रः। मायां प्रयोक्तुं समुपाजगाम बबन्ध तौ राजसुतौ दुरात्मा॥
answer: And when the son of the Rākşasa monarch felt himself incompetent to cope with them openly, then that impious one, resorting to illusion, bound those princes (by that means).

question: ततस्ताशरजालेन संनिवार्य महारथान्। पार्थः समन्तात् समरे प्रेषयमास मृत्यवे॥
answer: Then checking those mighty car-warriors with the net-work of arrows woven by himself, Partha began to dispatch them to the regions of Death.

question: यच्च त्वं मन्यसे प्राप्तं तद् ब्रवीहि सुयोधन। राधेय मन्यसे यच्च प्राप्तकालं वदाशु मे॥
answer: O Duryodhana, as this is the (proper) time, tell me, therefore, what is in your mind and also, in the mind of the son of Radha (Karna.)

question: ततो दुर्योधनादींस्तान् धार्तराष्ट्रान् महायशाः। तेनैव क्रमयोगेन जिज्ञासुः पर्यपृच्छत॥ अन्यांश्च शिष्यान् भीमादीन् राज्ञश्चैवान्यदेशजान्। तथा च सर्वे तत् सर्वं पश्याम इति कुत्सिताः॥
answer: Thereupon, the greatly illustrious (Drona) placed in the same position Duryodhana and other sons of Dhritarashtra and also Bhima and his other brothers and also all the princes that had come from other countries. He asked them one after another the some question, but they all replied as did Yudhisthira.

question: तदवस्थाप्यतां बुद्धिरलं देवि विकाङ्गया। विशोकं कुरु वैदेहि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्॥
answer: Do you therefore confide in me, O worshipful dame, and be not suspicious. And O Vaidehi, do you remove Rāma's grief as well as Laksmana's.

question: अस्मच्छुश्रूषणे नित्यं पिता हि निरतस्तव। आचष्टैतद्यथाख्यानं पिता ते त्वं तथा वद॥
answer: Your father was always ready to please us. Tell us, therefore, the story that your father had related.

question: एष पुत्रो महाप्रज्ञो वरुणस्येह गोपतेः। एष वै शीलवृत्तेन शौचेन च विशिष्यते॥
answer: This one is the son, of great wisdom, of Varuna the lord of the seas; he is specially famous for his holiness, his conduct and his ways of life.

question: एवं ब्रुवाणामरजां दण्डः कामवशं गतः। प्रत्युवाच मदोन्मत्तः शिरस्याधाय चाञ्जलिम्।।१३
answer: Arajas having said this, the king Danda, maddened with lust, placing folded palms on his head, said.

question: एव कारण्डवः पक्षी विगाह्य सलिलं शुभम्। रमन्ते कान्तया साधु काममुद्दीपयन्निव॥
answer: This swan, has been sporting with its mate in the lucid water of Pampă exciting my amour.

question: तन्त्रं चेदं विश्वरूपे युवत्यौ वयतस्तंतून्सततं वर्तयन्त्यौ। कृष्णान्सितांश्चैव विवर्तयन्त्यौ भूतान्यजस्रं भुवनानि चैव॥
answer: These maidens, representing the universe, are continually, weaving a cloth with white and black threads, creating innumerable words and millions of beings to inhabit them.

question: एप एव श्मशानेषु देवो वसति निर्दहन्। यजन्ते ते जनास्तत्र वीरस्थाननिषेविणः॥
answer: This great god loves to live in crematoria and there he burns and consumes all dead bodies. Those persons who celebrate sacrifices on such grounds attain at the end to the regions of heroes.

question: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच संशोच्य तु महात्मानं भीष्मं भीमपराक्रमम्। किमकार्षुः परं तात कुरुः कालचोदिताः॥
answer: Dhritarashtra said O son, having bewailed the high-souled Bhima of terrific might, what did the Kurus, goaded by Destiny, do?

question: निवर्तयित्वा तु रथं केशवोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्। वाहयन्नेव तुरगान् गरुडानिलरंहसः॥
answer: Having turned the course of his car, but not having restrained his horses, that were as swift as either the Gaurda (the chief of the birds) or the wind, Keshava addressed Arjuna, saying

question: संहिताध्यायिना भाव्यं गृहे वै गृहमेधिना। नित्यं स्वाध्यायिना भाव्यं च चाध्ययनजीविना॥
answer: He should live, engaged in the study of the Samhitas, and remaining at home he should perform all the duties of a householder. He should always be given to the study of the Vedas, but be should never derive the means of livelihood from such study.

question: अथ तान् द्विरदः कश्चित् सुरेन्द्रद्विरदोपमः॥ अश्वत्थस्थोऽग्निरित्येवमाह देवान् भृगूद्वह।
answer: Then, O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, an elephant, as large and powerful as the elephant of Shakra addressed the gods, sayingAgni is now living within this Ashvattha tree!

question: सर्ववर्णाश्च जायन्ते सदा चैव च द्वापरे। महोत्साहा वीर्यवन्तः परस्परजयैषिणः॥
answer: O kings, when Dvapara comes in, all the four orders of men become capable of great exertions. They possess great energy and they desire to conquer one another.

question: संदर्शनेन पुरुषं जघन्यमपि चोदयेत्। आरम्भान् द्विषतां प्राज्ञः सर्वार्थाश्च प्रसूदयेत्॥
answer: A king should even sent a low person to ascertain the disposition and doings of his enemies. A wise king should frustrate all the attempts and objects of his enemies.

question: दशाश्वस्य सुतस्त्वासीद् राजा परमधार्मिकः। सत्ये तपसि दाने च यस्य नित्यं रतं मनः॥
answer: Dashashva's son, o king, was a pious prince whose mind was continually devoted to the practice of truth and charity and devotion.

question: तमास्थितः केशवसंगृहीतं कपिध्वजो गाण्डिवबाणपाणिः। धनुर्धरो यस्य समः पृथिव्यां न विद्यते नो भविता कदाचित्॥
answer: On this (grand) car, which was driven by Keshava (Krishna) stood the ape-bannered hero with Gandiva (bow) and arrows in his hand, a great bow man whose equal there is none of earth or none will be.

question: ये त्वत्र निहता राजन्नन्तरायोधनं प्रति। यथाकथंचित् पुरुषास्ते गतास्तूत्तरान् कुरून्॥
answer: The remaining warriors, that have anyhow been killed on the field of battle, have attained to the region of the Uttara Kuru.'

question: प्रवादः सत्यमेवायं त्वां प्रति प्रायशो नृप॥ पतिव्रतानां नाकस्मात्पतन्त्यश्रूणि भूतले।
answer: O kin, the saying, that the tears of chaste damsels do not uselessly fall on the ground, has been verified (here) forsooth.

question: सर्वभूतभवं ज्ञात्वा लिङ्गमर्चति यः प्रभोः। तस्मिन्नभ्यधिकां प्रीतिं करोति वृषभध्वजः॥
answer: Knowing the Phallic from of Siva to be the origin of all forms, the lord Kesava adores him. The god having the bull for him emblem entertains great respect for Kesava.

question: किं नु वक्ष्यामि मुनिषु कर्म चासत्कृतं प्रभो। कस्मिन्वा कारणे त्यक्ता राघवेण महात्मना॥
answer: What reply shall I offer to the ascetics when they shall ask me "Child, why has the highsouled Rāghava renounced you? What sin have you committed?"

question: । नार्हसीहासुखं वस्तुं सुखार्हा सुखवर्जिता। प्राप्नुह्यनुत्तमं सौख्यं मत्तस्त्वं मत्तगामिनि॥ स्वादून्यमृतकल्पानि पेयानि विविधानि च। पिबमाना मनोज्ञानि रममाणा यथासुखम्॥ भोगोपचारान् विविधान् सौभाग्यं चाप्यनुत्तमम्। पानं पिब महाभागे भोगैश्चानुत्तमैः शुभैः॥
answer: you endued with the gait of an elephant in ruttish state, as you are accustomed to happiness, though deprived of it now, it behoves you not to live here in misery; pray receive from me all kinds of excellent things contributing to your happiness. Eating delightful and dainty viands of various kinds with taste almost equal to ambrosia, and sporting at your sweet will, attain fortune and all the enjoyable articles of superior and excellent kind and drink and wine, O blessed one.

question: तच्च मे कृन्तते मर्म यन्न तस्य शिरो मया। निषादविषये क्षिप्तं जयद्रथशिरो यथा।॥
answer: This fact that I have not thrown his head, like that of Jayadratha, into the omissions of the Nisadhas, is corroding he core of my heart.

question: स त्वं न दुःखी दुःखस्य न सुखी सुसुखस्य च। स्मर्तुमिच्छसि कौन्तेय किमन्यद् दुःखविभ्रमात्॥ अथवा ते स्वभावोऽयं येन पार्थावकृष्यसे। दृष्ट्वा सभागतां कृष्णामेकवस्त्रां रजस्वलाम्। मिषतां पाण्डवेयानां न तस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छसि॥ प्रव्राजनं च नगरादजिनैश्च विवासनम्। महारण्यनिवासश्च न तस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छसि॥ जटासुरात् परिक्लेशश्चित्रसेनेन चाहवः। सैन्धवाच्च परिक्लेशो न तस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छसि॥
answer: But you, O son of Kunti, do nether wish to recall your sorrows nor your happiness, what else do you wish to recall barring this delusion of sorrow. Or, perchance, O son of Pritha, it is your innate nature, by which you are at present overpowered. You do not wish to recall to your mind the painful spectacle of Krishna standing in the hall of assembly with only one piece of cloth to cover her body, and while she was in her menses and before all the Pandavas. And it is not proper that you should brood over your departure from the city, and your exile with the hide of the antelope for your dress, and your wanderings in the great forest, nor should you recall to your mind the affliction from Jatasura, the fight with Chitrasena, and your troubles from the Saindhavas.

question: तमुवाच महाबाहुर्भीमसेनो भुजङ्गमम्। न च कुप्ये महासर्प न चात्मानं विगर्हये।।२५।
answer: Then the mighty-armed Bhimasena said ic the snake "O highly-energetic creature, I am neither angry nor do I blame myself,

question: एतेनैतन्महद् वैरं प्रसक्तं पाण्डवैः सह। वधाय मम पुत्राणामात्मनः सगणस्य च॥
answer: This fire of hostility with the Pandavas had been lighted by Shakuni, for the destruction of my children as also of himself and his followers ar relatives.

question: यथा गणाः प्रवर्धन्ते न भिद्यन्ते च भारत। अरींश्च विजिगीषन्ते सुहृदः प्राप्नुवन्ति च।॥
answer: I wish to hear how they may advance, how they may be attached to the person of the king, and how, O Bharata, they may subduing foes gain friends.

question: युधिष्ठिरस्तु राजर्षिरात्मकर्मापराधजम्। चिन्तयन् स महाबाहुर्धातृणां दुःखमुत्तमम्॥ न सुष्वाप सुखं राजा हृदि शल्यैरिवार्पितैः। दौरात्म्यमनुपश्यंस्तत् काले द्यूतोद्भवस्य हि॥
answer: That royal sage, the illustrious Yudhishthira, reflecting that the extremity of misery which had befallen his brothers was owing to his own fault and remembering also the sufferings that had arisen from his act of gambling, could not sleep in peace. He felt as if his heart had been pierced with a lance.

question: दिष्ट्या त्वामिह संग्रामादस्माद् वीरक्षयात् पुरम्॥ समागतमपश्याम ांशुमन्तमिव प्रजाः।
answer: By good luck we see you alive in this terrible battle in which heroes have been killed like creatures beholding the blazing sun.

question: यां योगिनो ध्यानविविक्तदर्शनाः प्रयान्ति यां चोत्तमयज्विनो जनाः। तपोभिरिद्धैरनुयान्ति यां तथा तामक्षया ते तनयो गतो गतिम्॥
answer: Your son has ascended to those regions, the eternal goal of Yogins who contemplate with their eyes shut or by performers of illustrious sacrifices or by people possessed of great ascetic merit.

question: आत्मसंयमनं बुद्ध्या परबुद्ध्यावधारणम्। बुद्ध्या चात्मगुणप्राप्तिरेतच्छास्त्रनिदर्शनम्॥
answer: By dint of his own intelligence, he should determine what he is to do. By consulting with others he should either leave off or conform such resolution. Helped by that intelligence which is sharpened by the scriptures, one can fix his courses of action. Herein consists the utility of the scriptures.

question: यस्य चैतद् व्रतं मह्यं वधे किल दुरात्मनः। पादौ न धावये तावद् यावद्धन्यां न फाल्गुनम्॥ मृषा कृत्वा व्रतं तस्य पापस्य मधुसूदन। पातयिष्ये रथात् कायं शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
answer: And such was the vow of that wretch of human beings about taking my life, that "until I put an end to the existence of Phalguna, I will not have my feet washed.” Giving a lie to the words of honor of that vile creature, O Madhusudan, I will, hitting him straight with my arrows, throw off his body from his car.

question: स वै शाकरसं दृष्ट्वा हर्षाविष्टः प्रनृत्तवान्। ततस्तस्मिन् प्रनृत्ते वै स्थावरं जङ्गमं च यत्॥
answer: Seeing that vegetable juice, the Rishi was filled with joy and danced about there. Beholding him dance, all mobile and immobile creatures, O hero, overpowered by his energy, began to dance.

question: न च सीतां दशग्रीवः प्राप्नोति जनकात्मजाम्। बद्धं बलवता वैरमक्षयं राघवेण च ॥
answer: But he could not spread his influence upon Sitā the daughter of king Jannak and deep rooted and eternal became the enmity with the highly powerful Rāghava.

question: मायां च राक्षसी कृत्वा शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्। तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम शैनेयस्य पराक्रमम्॥
answer: Spreading an illusion through his Rakshasas prowess, he covered Satyaki with an arrow downpour. Then we did behold the wonderful prowess of the grandson of Shini.

question: अध्रुवे जीवलोके च स्थाने वा शाश्वते सति। जीविते मरणान्ते च कस्माच्छोचसि भारत॥
answer: When this life is fickle, when this word itself is not eternal, when life is sure to end in death, why then, O Bharata, do you grieve?

question: शिखण्डी तु भृशं राजस्ताङ्यमानः शितैः शरैः। आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं माधवस्य महात्मनः॥
answer: Thus wounded sore with sharp arrows, Shikhandin quickly ascended, O monarch, the car of the high-souled Satyaki, that scion of the dynasty of Madhu.

question: अहेरिव गणाद् भीतः सौहित्यानरकादिव। कुणपादिव च स्त्रीभ्यस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
answer: The gods regard him as a Brahmana who fears company like a snake; the full measure of gratification (from foods and drinks) as of hell; and women as a corpse.

question: इन्द्र उवाच मा भेस्त्वं शीघ्रमेतद् वै कुरुष्व वचनं मम। मत्प्रसादाद्धि ते शस्त्रं वज्रकल्पं भविष्यति॥
answer: Shakra said You need not have any fears, do quickly what I tell you; through my favour shall your weapon be equal to the thunderbolt.

question: स त्वां निहतमाक्रन्दे श्रुत्वा संतापतापितः। नियम्य दिव्यान्यस्राणि नायुध्यत यथा पुरा॥
answer: Withdrawing his celestial weapons he ceased to fight. Beholding him greatly anxious and overpowered with grief.

question: न त्वेतदकुलीनासु नाधर्मिष्ठासु विद्यते। यद् ब्राह्मणार्थं विसृजेदात्मानमपि चात्मजम्॥
answer: Even those that are lowly born and sinful refuse to do this; one should sacrifice himself and children for the sake of a Brahmana.

question: कच्चित् सौते न ते मोहः शाल्वं दृष्ट्वा महाहवे। विषादो वा रणं दृष्ट्वा ब्रूहि में त्वं यथातथम्॥
answer: O son of Suta, have you been bewildered at the sight of Shalva in that great battle? Have you been disheartened at the sight of the battle? Tell me truly your mind.

question: अविद्या कर्म तृष्णा च केचिदाहुः पुनर्भवे। कारणं लोभमोहौ तु दोषाणां तु निषेवणम्॥
answer: Some hold that there is re-birth which is caused by Ignorance, the desire for acts, cupidity, carelessness, and bent towards other vices.

question: भ्रामयन्तं कपिं दृष्ट्वा सालवृक्षं महाबलम्। चिक्षेप सुबहून्बाणाञ्जम्बुमाली महाबलः॥
answer: Seeing the exceedingly strong monkey whirling the Sāla tree, the highly powerful Jambumālī dischanged a many shafts.

question: स पश्चिमेन द्वारेण निर्ययौ राक्षसैर्वृतः। इन्द्रजित्सुमहावीर्य: पौलस्त्यो देवकण्टकः॥
answer: That highly powerful, Indrajit, a descendant of Pulasta and an enemy of the celestials, issued out, encircled by the Rākşasas, by the western gate.

question: ते तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य राक्षसाः। जग्मुः परमसंभ्रान्ताः कुम्भकर्णनिवेशनम्॥
answer: Hearing the words of the lord of the Rākşasas, the Rākşasas, bestirring themselves, went to the abode of Kumbhakarņa.

question: सुवर्णपुजैर्नाराचैर्बलवन्तौ कृतव्रणौ। प्रसुनुवाते रुधिरं कीर्तिमन्तौ जये धृतौ॥
answer: And pierced with närâchas knobbed with gold, those-powerful and illustrious (warriors) with their hearts set on celebrity, bled profusely.

question: स्वभावस्तु प्रयात्यग्रे प्रभवन्त्यशनान्यपि। द्वन्द्वानि च विरुद्धानि तानि सर्वाण्यचिन्तयन्॥
answer: Nature always walks before : hence, food and drink will somehow come. I shall not think of those pairs of opposites that are inimical to such a life.

question: तस्मिन्प्रतिहतेऽस्त्रे तु राघवेण महात्मना। रावणः क्रोधताम्राक्षः सौरमस्त्रमुदरीयत्॥
answer: On that weapon being baffled by the highsouled Raghava, Rävaņa, with his eyes rendered coppery with passion took up a Solar weapon.

question: अश्वत्थामेति हि गजः ख्यातो नाम्ना हतोऽभवत्। कृत्वा मनसि तं भीमो मिथ्या व्याहृतवांस्तदा॥
answer: The elephant known by the name of Ashvatthaman having been slain, Bhima spoke of Ashvatthainan's death. Knowing the true fact in his mind, Bhima then spoke what was false.

question: तस्मिंश्च गतमात्रेऽथ राजा गौरमुखे तदा। मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रयामास सह संविग्नमानसः॥
answer: When Gaurmukha had gone away the king in great anxiety consulted with all his ministers without delay.

question: एतेनैवानुमानेन मन्यन्ते वै मनीषिणः। सत्त्वं च पुरुषश्चैव तत्र नास्ति विचारणा॥
answer: It is by this inference that the wise believe in the oneness of Purusha and Goodness. There is no doubt in this.

question: कृतानि वेश्मानि च पाण्डुराणि तथा सुपुष्पाण्यपि पुष्कराणि। पुनश्च पद्मानि सकेसराणि वनानि चित्राणि सरोवराणि ॥
answer: And (in it), where white mansions were reared, there were tank's filed with fair flowers; and lotuses furnished with filaments; and picturesque woods; and liquid lapses.

question: हैडिम्बाश्च महावीर्यो विहगो मद्बलोपमः। वहेदनघ सर्वान्नो वचनात् ते घटोत्कचः॥
answer: O sinless one, at your command, the son of Hidimba, Ghatotkacha, who can range the skies and who is as strong as myself will carry us all.

question: ब्राह्मणा: कुरुमुख्यस्य ये मुक्ता हयसारिणः। कुर्वन्ति शान्ति कामस्य रणे योऽयं मया हतः॥
answer: What benefit is done to this hero, killed by me in battle, by those Brahmanas who were commissioned to attend upon this foremost one of Kuru's race engaged in following the horse?

question: इन्येवमुक्त्वा नृपते धनंजयसुतो नृपः। उपस्पृश्याभवत् तूष्र्णी प्रायोपेतो महामतिः॥
answer: Having bewailed thus, the great son of Dhananjaya, king Babhruvahana, touched water and became silent, vowing to starve himself to death.

question: राज्ञस्त्वनन्तरो राजा पाञ्चाल्यो दुपदोऽभवत्। जातरूपमयच्छत्रः सर्वैस्तैरभिरक्षितः॥
answer: After king Yudhishthira, came Drupada, the ruler of the Panchalas, with a golden umbrella held over his head and himself protected by all those soldiers.

question: नि:स्वाध्यायवषट्कारं नष्टयज्ञोत्सवक्रियम्। जगदासीनिरुत्साहं कालेयभयपीडितम्॥
answer: The universe, being afflicted with the terror of the Kalkeyas and being destitute of the Vedic studies, of the Vashats and the sacrificial festivals and religious rites, became very fearless.

question: तमस्त्वतीव विस्तीर्णं मोह आविशतीव माम्। संज्ञां नोपलभे सूत मनो विह्वलतीव मे॥
answer: Utter darkness is all around me, a faintness comes over me. O Suta, consciousness is leaving me, my mind is distracted.

question: तेषु योधसहस्रेषु तावकेषु परेषु च। एको दुर्योधनो ह्यासीत् पुमानिति मतिर्मम॥
answer: Amongst those thousands of warriors on the field, of your side or that of the enemy, it appeared as if Duryodhana was then the only man.

question: तत्राधिरथिभीमाभ्यां शरैर्मुक्तैर्दढे हताः। इषुपातमतिक्रम्य पेतुरश्चनरद्विपाः॥
answer: As Karna and Bhima, desirous of baffling each other shot numerous arrows, many elephants, horses and men, wounded therewith, fell down dead;

question: भारद्वाजं त्रिभिर्बाणैर्दुःसहं नवभिः शरैः। विकर्णे पञ्चविंशत्या चित्रसेनं च सप्तभिः॥
answer: Satyaki pierced the son of Bharadvaja with three arrows, Dussaha with nine, Vikarna with twenty-five, Chitrasena with seven.

question: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। एकान्ते योजयित्वाश्वान् प्रायादभिमुखः परान्॥
answer: Sanjaya continued “Having said so, O king, the brave son of Drona yoked his horses to his car at a corner and started towards the direction of his enemies.

question: रोषात् प्रस्फुरमाणोष्ठः सुग्रीवं प्रति लक्ष्मणः। ददर्श वानरान् भीमान् किष्किन्धायां बहिश्चरान्॥
answer: And having his lips swollen with anger for Sugrīva, Lakşmaņa beheld the terrible monkeys walking outside the city.

question: तमब्रवीत् तथा शङ्खस्तीव्ररोषसमन्वितः। स्तेयं त्वया कृतमिदं फलान्याददता स्वयम्॥
answer: Filled with great anger, Shankha said to him,—You have committed theft by taking yourself these fruits.

question: भारद्वाजस्ततस्तूर्ण पाण्डवानां महाचमूम्। दारयामास समरे शतथोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ शिखण्डी तु महाराज द्रौणिमासाद्य संयुगे। आजधान भ्रुवोर्मध्ये नाराचैस्त्रिभिराशुगैः॥
answer: Thereafter in that battle, the son of Bharadvaja resisted, by hundreds and by thousand the mighty army belonging to the sons of Pandu. Shikhandin also, O mighty sovereign encountering the son of Drona in the conflict, wounded him between the brows with three swift coursing long shafts.

question: सा छिन्ना बहुभिर्बाणैर्धारद्वाजेन मारिष। गदा पपात कौरव्य नादयन्ती धरातलम्॥
answer: Cut off by numerous shafts by the son of Bharadvaja that mace, O sire, fell down, ) Kaurava, filling the earth with the noise it created.

question: भक्त्या रामस्य ये चेमा संहितामृषिणा कृताम्। ये लिखन्तीह च नरास्तेषां वासस्त्रिविष्टपे॥
answer: Those, who shall write this story of Rāma first recorded by the Rși (Vālmīki) shall reach the region of Brahma.

question: कच्चित् सुकुशलं राजैल्लोकानां राक्षसाधिप। आशङ्के नाधिजाने त्वं यतस्तूर्णमुपागतः॥
answer: O king, O lord of the Rākşasas, is it well with the worlds? I am filled with fear: I apprehend that all is not right, since you have come hither (alone) in such post-haste speed.

question: तस्माद् दातव्यमेवेह प्रतिश्रुत्य युधिष्ठिर। यदीच्छेच्छोभनां जाति प्राप्तुं भरतसत्तम॥
answer: Therefore, O Yudhishthira, if one wishes to come by a respectable or happy order of being in his next birth, he should, having made the promise to a Brahmana, certainly satisfy it by actually making the gift to him.

question: यदास्थितो रथं दिव्यं पदान चलितः पदम्। देवराजोऽपि हि मया नित्यमत्रोपलक्षितः॥ विचलन् प्रथमोत्पाते हयानां भरतर्षभ। त्वं पुनः स्थित एवात्र रथे भ्रान्ते कुरूद्वह॥
answer: That placed in this celestials car you are not jerked even a step from your seat. O best of the Bharatas, I have often noticed that (even) the king of the gods is unable to keep up his balance at the first pull by the horses. O perpetuator of the Kuru race, your sitting (steadily) in the car while in motion,

question: अपश्यमानः स तु तां बहु तत्र विलप्य च। निश्चेष्टः पार्थिवश्रेष्ठो मुहूर्तं स व्यतिष्ठत॥
answer: Having failed to find her, that best of kings gave vent to much lamentations and he remained motionless in grief for sometime.

question: वृणोमि कीर्ति लोके हि जीवितेनापि भानुमन्। कीर्तिमानश्नुते स्वर्ग हीनकीर्तिस्तु नश्यति॥
answer: O Brahmana, I long for renown in this world even at the sacrifice of my life. Men having renown attain to heaven while those having none are lost.

question: अध्यगा नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिं कुतस्त्वामिदमागतम्। एतदाचक्ष्व मे सर्वं निखिलेन महामते॥
answer: But how have you gained this stability of understanding? How have you gained this knowledge? O you of great intelligence, tell me all this fully.

question: आविशन्ति च यं यक्षाः पुरुषं कालपर्यये। उन्माद्यति स तु क्षिप्रं ज्ञेयो यक्षग्रहस्तु सः।।५३
answer: When a Yaksha spirit by some means or other enters the body of a human being, he immediately turns mad. Such a spirit is called the Yaksha spirit.

question: ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु। बले तस्मिन्निपतिता माहेन्द्रा इव केतवः॥
answer: And burnt up by its energy, the most of Vaivasvata fell down in the field like to banners of Mahendra.

question: मच्छरैरग्निसंकाशैविद्धदेहान् सहस्रशः। इत्येवं ब्रुवतस्तस्य सात्यकेरमितौजसः॥
answer: And mangled, by my sharp shafts whose touch resemble that of fire itself.” When Satyaki of immeasurable prowess was thus speaking.

question: यस्तु वेद निराधारं ज्ञानं नत्त्वविनिश्चयात्। सर्वभूनस्थमात्मानं स सर्वगतिरिष्यते॥
answer: He who understands self through accurate determination of all subjects, undisturbed, which is at one with Knowledge, and which lives in all principles, succeeds in going everywhere.

question: घटोत्कच उवाच अलमेवास्मि कर्णाय द्रोणायालं च भारत। अन्येषां क्षत्रियाणां च कृतास्राणां महात्मनाम्॥
answer: Ghatotkacha said I am capable of encountering Karna and Drona, O Bharata and I am a match for all the other high-souled Kshatriyas accomplished in the use of weapons.

question: आर्यस्याज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य विसृज्य जनकात्मजाम्। गङ्गातीरे यथोद्दिष्टे वाल्मीकेराश्रमे शुभे।८॥ तत्र तां च शुभाचारामाश्रमान्ते यशस्विनीन्। पुनरप्यागतो वीरपादमूलमुपासितुम्॥
answer: O worshipful sir, having obeyed your behest's I have left the daughter of Janaka at the holy hermitage of Vālmiki near the banks of the Gangā. Having left that illustrious pure lady at the skirt of the hermitage. I have again come to serve your feet

question: सर्वानेताननादृत्य दुर्मतिर्निरपत्रपः। अशिष्टवदमर्यादो मानी मान्यावमानिता।॥
answer: Disregarding all these that shameless one of wicked intellect, like a dishonorable man, vain and yet not commanding respect and given to insulting those who ought to be respected, went out of the court.

question: शृणुमैथिलि मद्वाक्यं मासान् द्वादश भामिनि ॥ कालेनानेन नाभ्येषि यदि मां चारुहासिनि। ततस्त्वां प्रातराशार्थं सूदाश्छेत्स्यन्ति लेशशः॥
answer: Hear, O Maithili, my words. O damsel if, O you of sweet smiles, within this time you do not turn yourself to me, the cooks shall cut you off in pieces to serve my morning mcal.

question: ददर्श स तदा गावः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। अङ्कुर्लक्षैश्च ताः सर्वा लक्षयामास पार्थिवः॥
answer: The king saw his cattle by hundreds and thousands. Examining their limbs and marks, he supervised their counting.

question: गान्धार्युवाच अध्यर्धगुणमाहुर्यं बले शौर्ये च केशव। पित्रा त्वया च दाशार्ह दृप्तं सिंहमिवोत्कटम्। यो बिभेद चमूमेको मम पुत्रस्य दुर्भिदाम्। स भूत्वा मृत्युरन्येषां मम पुत्रस्य मृत्युवशं गतः॥
answer: Gandhari said He whose power and bravery were regarded, O Keshava, as a one and half times superior to those of his father and you, he who took after a dreadful and proud, lion, he who alone pierced the impenetrable army of my son, he who killed many, alas, he now sleeps there, himself dead.

question: छित्त्वा तु तानाशु चैव कङ्कपत्रशिलाशितान्॥ एकैकमेषां समरे बिभेद निशितैः शरैः।
answer: Having off those sharp arrows bedecked with Kanka-feathers, Arjuna pierced each of the warriors opposed to him with a whetted arrow.

question: सेनाग्रगा मन्त्रिसुताः किंकरा रावणात्मजः। एते हनुमता तत्र एकेन वितिपातिताः।।६।
answer: What to speak of more, Hanuman, singlehanded, slew Ravana's commander-in-chief, the minister's son, his servants and his one son.

question: दक्षिणं दक्षिणं काले सम्भृत्य स्वभुजं तदा। हस्तिहस्तोपमं शैक्षं सर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम्॥ प्रगृह्णन्नञ्जलीन् नृणामुद्यतान् सर्वतो दिशः। शुश्राव मधुरा वाचो नानादेशनिवासिनाम्॥
answer: Followed and surrounded by his uterine brother, he proceeded, raising his right arm sinewy like the trunk of the elephant and capable of crushing all his foes, and therewith accepting the homage's offered by men on all sides with their raised and folder palms.

question: सुवर्णकार्णायसवर्मनद्धा नागा यता हैमवता: प्रवृद्धाः। तथा स शत्रून् समरे विनिघ्नन्। गाण्डीवधन्वा पुरुषप्रवीरः॥
answer: Like huge Himalaya elephants dressed with armours made of black steel decked with gold. Thus slaying his enemies in battle that heroic man, the holder of Gandiva bow,

question: किमन्यद् राक्षसानन्यानस्मांश्च परिभूय ह। तमहं सगणं राजन् सवाजिरथकुञ्जरम्॥ हैडिम्बि च सहामात्यं हन्तुमभ्यागतः स्वयम्। अद्य कुन्तीसुतान् सर्वान् वासुदेवपुरोगमान्॥ हत्वा सम्भक्षयिष्यामि सर्वैरनुचरैः सह। निवारय बलं सर्वं वयं योत्स्याम पाण्डवान्॥
answer: Utterly disregarding ourselves and other Rakshasas. What shall I say more, O king, I have now come of my own accord here to slay him with his followers and cars and steeds and elephants as also the son of Hidimba with all his counselors. Today slaying all the sons of Kunti, headed by the son of Vasudeva, I will eat them up in company with all my followers. Prevent all your troops from battle with the Pandavas; we will fight with them."

question: महत्प्रधानभूतस्य गुणोऽहंकार एव च॥ अहंकारात् तु सम्भूतो महाभूतकृतो गुणः।
answer: A development of Pradhana when it has become Mahat is Egoism. From egoism emanates the great elements.

question: किं नावबुध्यसे क्रूरे नियतं बन्धुसंश्रयम्। ज्येष्ठं पितृसमं रामं कौसल्यायात्मसम्भवम्॥
answer: Does you not, O tortuous one, know that that one sprung from Kucalya's, self, my eldest brother Räma, who is like a father to me, has ever been the refuge of his friends?

question: बलप्रयत्नादधिरूढवेगां मन्त्रैश्च घोरैरभिमन्त्र्य यत्नात्। ससर्ज मार्गेण च तां परेण वधाय मद्राधिपतेस्तदानीम्॥
answer: Having inspired it with many mantras and impregnated it with terrible velocity by the exercise of great power and care, king Yudhishthira hurled it by the best path for the destruction of the king of the Madras.

question: स गत्वा तु यधोद्देशं पाण्डवान् ददृशे वने। जनन्या सह कौरव्य मापयानान् नदीजलम्॥
answer: He went to the place where he was directed to go; and he was the descendants of Kuru, the son of Pandu, with their mother, measuring the depth of the water of a river in the forest.

question: शत्रोरपि प्रपन्नस्य सोऽनृशंसः प्रतापवान्। दाताभयस्य बीभत्सुरमितात्मा महाबलः॥
answer: The high-souled and Immeasurably powerful Vivatsu shows mercy and extends protection even to an enemy when he is fallen.

question: दुर्योधन उवाच नाह भवति न द्रोणे नाश्वत्थाम्नि न संजये। न भीष्मे न च काम्बोजे न कृपे न च बाह्निके॥ सत्यव्रते पुरुमित्रे भूरिश्रवसि वा पुनः। अन्येषु वा तावकेषु भारं कृत्वा समाह्वयम्॥
answer: Duryodhana said I do not depend on Drona or Ashvathama or Sanjaya or Bhishma or Kamboja or Kripa or Balhika or Satyavrata or Purumitra or on Bhurishravas, nor do I challenge them to fight, depending on others.

question: कृपश्च सोमदत्तश्च बाह्रीकश्च महामनाः॥ ततोऽहमब्रुवं तत्र विदुरेण प्रचोदितः।
answer: Kripa, Somadatta, and the high souled Valhika. It was then at the advice of Vidura, I spoke thus (to Draupadi).

question: भीष्मे द्रोणे कृपे कर्णे द्रोणपुत्रे जयद्रथे। भूयसी वर्तते वृत्तिं न शमे कुरुते मनः॥
answer: He has too great a confidence on Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Karna, the son of Drona and Jayadratha and therefore he does not think of peace.

question: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सैन्येषु ये चारपुरुषा मम। ते प्रवृत्तिं प्रयच्छन्ति ममेमां व्युषितां निशाम्॥
answer: Yudhishthira said The spies, whom I have in the army of the son of Dhritarashtra, brought me this news when the night has passed away.

question: प्रद्युम्नादनिरुद्धं त्वं यं विदुर्विष्णुमव्ययम्। अनिरुद्धोऽसृजन्मां वै ब्रह्माणं लोकधारिणम्॥
answer: From Pradyumana you did then create Anirudha known as the undetiorating Vishnu. And it was Anirudha who did create me Brahman as the supporter of the universe.

question: संश्रितं चापि यस्त्यक्त्वा साधुं तद्वचने रतम्। न विभर्ति नृशंसात्मा निन्दते चोपकारिणम्॥ अर्हते प्रातिवेश्याय श्राद्धं यो न ददाति च। अनर्हेभ्यश्च यो दद्याद् वृषलीपतये तथा॥ मद्यपो भिन्नमर्यादः कृतघ्नो भर्तृनिन्दकः। तेषां गतिमियां क्षिप्रं न चेद्धन्यां जयद्रथम्॥
answer: That end which overtakes the cruel-hearted wretch who without maintaining a pious and sons obedient protege casts him off or him who without giving a deserving neighbour the offerings in a sraddha, gives them to one undeserving of them; that end that overtakes them who accept in marriage Vrishalis; that end which becomes his who indulges in wine, his who contemns those that are worthy of veneration or his who is ungrateful or his who speaks evil of his brethren, that end shall also soon overtake me if I do not slay Jayadratha.

question: सात्यकिस्तु रणे क्रुद्धो मोहयित्वा सुतं तव॥ शरैरग्निशिखाकारैराजघान स्तनान्तरे। त्रिभिरेव महाभागः शरैः संनतपर्वभि।
answer: Thereat Satyaki waxing wroth, stupefied your son and struck him on the centre of his chest with arrows resembling tongues of fire.

question: विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा कथान्ते रघुनन्दनः। उवाच परमप्रीतो मुनि दीप्तमिवानलम्॥
answer: When Viśvāmitra had ended, hearing his words, Rāma exceedingly pleased, spoke to that ascetic resembling flaming fire, saying,

question: ततोऽहं त्वामनुप्राप्तः नैतदौपयिकं राजंस्त्वयि भीष्मे च जीवति। यदन्योन्येन ते पुत्रा विरुध्यन्ते कथंचन॥
answer: O king, when yourself and Bhishma are (still) alive, it is not proper that your sons should quarrel amongst themselves.

question: विचित्रवीर्यं च तदा बालमप्राप्तयौवनम्। कुरुराज्ये महाबाहुरभ्यषिञ्चदनन्तरम्॥
answer: Thereupon, he installed the mighty armed boy Vichitravirya, still in his minority, on the throne of the Kuru kingdom.

question: ब्रह्मदेयाग्रहारांश्च पुत्राणामौर्ध्वदेहिकम्। इतो रत्नानि गाश्चैव दासीदासमजाविकम्॥ आनयित्वा कुरुश्रेष्ठो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छतु। दीनान्धकृपणेभ्यश्च तत्र तत्र नृपाज्ञया॥
answer: Let the foremost one of the Kuru race give away for the obsequial rites of his sons, all those foremost of gifts which should be given to the Brahmanas. Indeed, let him make those gifts to persons of the twice-born caste, taking away from our places jewels, gems, and kine, and slaves both male and female, and goats and sheep. Let gifts be made to also those who are poor or blind or in great distress, selecting the objects of his charity as he likes.

question: गोमायुरुवाच सदृशं मृगराजैतत् तव वाक्यं मदन्तरे। यत् सहायान् मृगयसे धर्मार्थकुशलाशुचीन्॥
answer: The jackal said O king of beasts, these words of yours about myself are such as become you. It is also becoming of you that you should cock for ministers of pure conduct and who conversant with duties and worldly affairs,

question: आविध्य भीमोऽपि गदां सुघोरां विचिक्षिपे रोषपरीतमूर्तिः। सा तस्य शक्तिं सहसा विरुज्य पुत्रं तवाजौ ताडयामास मूर्ध्नि॥
answer: Bhima fomenting in rage giving turns to his fearful mace struck his enemy with it. Crushing Dusasana's dart, that mace came down straight on your son and hit on the head.

question: प्रणिपातप्रसन्ना हि मैथिली जनकात्मजा॥ अलमेषा परित्रातुं राक्षस्यो महतो भयात्।
answer: Propitiated by our bowing down, Janaka's daughter, Maithili, shall rescue the Raksasis from a mighty fear."

question: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः प्रतीपो राजाऽऽसीत् सर्वभूतहितः सदा। निषसाद समा बह्वीर्गङ्गाद्वारगतो जपन्॥
answer: Vaishampayana said: There was a king, named Pratipa, engaged in doing good to all creatures. He spent many years in ascetic penances, going to the source of (the river)Ganga.

question: तया विहीनः कृपणः कथं लक्ष्मण धारये। या मामनुगता राज्याद् भ्रष्टं विहतचेतसम्॥
answer: How shall I keep up (my being) being poorly, O Lakşmaņa, being forsaken by that Sītā who followed me, deprived of kingdom and sense?

question: तेषां तु रुदतां शब्दात् प्रतिशब्दोऽभवद् गिरौ। भ्रातृणां सह वैदेह्या सिंहानां नर्दतामिव ॥
answer: And there the hill reverberated at the sounds raised by the brothers wailing along with Vaidehi; like to lions roaring.

question: यद्यधर्मो भवेद्भूतो रावणो नरकं व्रजेत्। भवांश्च धर्मसंयुक्तो नैव व्यसनमाप्नुयात्॥
answer: If unrighteousness would bring unhappiness on creatures, Ravana should hence to hell, and you possessed of virtue, should not come by misfortune.

question: नष्टमात्मनि संलीनं नाधिजग्मुर्हताशनम्। ततः संजातसंत्रासानग्निदर्शनलालसान्॥ जलेचरः क्लान्तमनास्तेजसाग्नेः प्रदीपितः। उवाच देवान् मण्डूको रसातलतलोत्थितः॥ रसातलतले देवा वसत्यग्निरिति प्रभो। संतापादिह सम्प्राप्तः पावकप्रभवादहम्॥
answer: They could not find out the eater of sacrificial libations who had concealed himself by merging his self into self. At this time, a frog, living in water, got on the surface from the nethermost regions, with cheerless heart on account of having been scorched by the energy of Agni. The little creature addressed the celestials who had become stricken with fear and who had became stricken with fear and who were all very eager to see the god of fire, saying, You gods, Agni is now living in the nethermost regions. Scorched by the energy of that god and unable to bear in longer, I have come here.

question: युधिष्ठिरस्तु कौन्तेयो बभूवास्वस्थचेतनः। अनिष्टदर्शनान् घोरानुत्पातान् परिचिन्तयन्॥
answer: On the other hand, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, beholding and thinking of terrible ill omens became uneasy.

question: शैनेयाभ्युपपत्तिं ते जानाम्याचार्यघातिनि। न चैनं त्रास्यसि मया ग्रस्तमात्मानमेव च॥
answer: O grandson of Shini, I know the partiality you bear for the murderer of his preceptor (viz., Dhristadyumna), but you shall not succeed in saying him and your own self when assailed by me.

question: उत्थितः स ह्रदाद् स तुद्यमानो बलवान् वाग्मी रामसमन्ततः॥ वीरः प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्।
answer: Cut with wordy darts, O Rama, from every side, the powerful and heroic Duryodhana has risen from the lake, armed with his heavy inace.

question: हरेत् कीर्ति धर्ममस्योपरुर्ध्या दर्थे दीर्घ वीर्यमस्योपहन्यात्। रिपुढेष्टा दुर्बलो वा बली वा तस्माच्छनोनॆव हीयेद् यतात्मा॥
answer: An enemy, strong or weak, impelled by malice, may very soon destroy the fame of a king, impede the acquisition of religious merit by him; and deprive him of even his energy. Therefore, a king, who is of a controlled mind, should never be careless when he has an enemy.

question: स्वस्रीयं वासुदेवस्य पुत्रं गाण्डीवधन्वनः। कथं त्वातिरथं वीरं द्रक्ष्याम्यद्य निपातितम्॥
answer: How shall we see you slain, you who are the son of the wielder of the Gandiva, the son of Vasudeva's sister, you who are a hero and a Atiratha too!

question: यो जात: कवची खड्गी सशरः सशरासनः। सुसमिद्धे महाबाहुः पावके पावकोपमः॥
answer: Who rose as a mighty-armed hero with natural armour, sword, bow and arrows from the blazing fire, himself looking like a second fire.

question: कथं वास्मासु जीवत्सु त्वयि चैव जनार्दन। हैडिम्बिः प्राप्तवान् मृत्युं सूतपुत्रेण सङ्गतः॥
answer: How is it, O Janardana, that Hidimva's son met with death in his encounter with Suta's son, although you and ourselves are still alive?

question: ते कृत्वा समरव्यूहं सूचीमुखमरिंदमाः। बिभिदुर्धार्तराष्ट्राणां तद् स्थानीकमाहवे॥
answer: Those grinders of foes forming their troops in the array known as Suchimukha, penetrated, in that battle, into that car-division of the sons of Dhritarashtra.

question: दिष्ट्या जयसि कौरव्य दिष्ट्या भीष्मो निपातितः॥२८ अवध्यो मानुषैरेव सत्यसंधो महारथः।
answer: “Through good fortune, O best of the Kurus, have you attained victory; through good fortune has Bhishma, that mighty car-warrior of unerring aim, incapable of being slain by men, been overthrown.

question: योगो योग इति प्रीत्या ततः शब्दो महानभूत्। क्रोशतां सादिनां तत्र युज्यतां युज्यतामिति॥
answer: Immediately loud clamour consisting of the words, 'Equip, Equip'! of horse-men, O Bharata, engaged in equipping their horses.

question: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तस्तदा रामो जहि भीष्ममिति प्रभो। उवाच रुदती कन्यां चोदयन्तीं पुनः पुनः॥
answer: Bhishma said “O Rama, slay Bhishma, “having been thus addressed, my lord, he said to that weeping girl who urged him again and again.

question: तामापतन्तीं भरतानुजोस्त्रैर्जधान बाणैश्च हुताग्निकल्पैः। तथापि सा तस्य विवेश शक्तिर्भुजान्तरं दाशरथेविशालम्॥
answer: As it coursed on, Bharata's younger brother resisted it with arrows resembling a sacrificial flame. Yet the dart pierced into the broad arm of Dasaratha's son.

question: ते समुद्रेषु गिरिषु वनेषु च सरस्सु च। वानरा वानरान् सर्वान् रामहेतोरचोदयन्॥
